serendipity_bridge.synthesis_notes: Explaining recursive boundary logic step by step can help a person notice gaps in their reasoning.

core_essence.foundation: For a complex parameter c, start with z0 = 0 and iterate z(n+1) = z(n)^2 + c. The Mandelbrot set contains the values of c for which this sequence remains bounded.
core_essence.philosophical_anchor: Intricate structure emerges from a simple iterative rule near the boundary between bounded and unbounded behavior.
core_essence.functional_role: A project-design metaphor for exploring boundaries, scale, and iterative feedback; it does not supply an engineering algorithm.

scale_invariance.definition: The set has recurring structure across zoom levels, including approximate self-similarity in some regions; it is not uniformly identical at every scale.
scale_invariance.project_application: Use as a prompt to check whether local tasks align with broader project principles.

liminal_boundary.definition: The set's boundary separates parameters with bounded iteration from those with unbounded iteration and has fractal structure.
liminal_boundary.project_application: Use as a metaphor for marking experiment limits and explicit rollback conditions.

iterative_feedback.definition: Repeatedly applying a rule, with each output becoming the next input.
iterative_feedback.project_application: Use as a metaphor for review cycles; project changes still require human decisions and tests.

cross_reference_links.synergy: A shared rule system can be used as a metaphor for structure across levels.
Stepwise explanation can help make recursive assumptions explicit.

adventure_quests.title: The Boundary Exploration Protocol
adventure_quests.objective: Map project risks and experimental ideas against stability and rollback boundaries.
adventure_quests.outcome: Documented distinction between stable core and experiments.
